## Documentation is not code integration

- This checkpoint publishes documentation only. It does not integrate compatibility code, the canonical ledger, or the upstream release baseline into develop.
- Batch source hashes identify coverage obligations. Their status remains authoritative only in the canonical ledger at the recorded ledger revision.
- The historical classifier is not a progress report and must not be regenerated from this file.
- Local commits are unavailable to other clones until someone explicitly pushes them. Stable promotion, publishing, and deployment remain outside this campaign.
- Before resuming, inspect the named Git revisions and current review evidence. Do not assume an agent or isolated environment is still running.

## Required handoff for every batch

Use the [playbook's batch record and review workflow](t3-upstream-import-playbook.md#review-and-ledger-workflow).
Before implementation, record the ordered full source hashes, target, starting
revision, true prerequisites, execution ordering, excluded changes, Pulse
preservation tests, affected clients and providers, connection modes, and scoped
checks. Record partial prerequisite adoption explicitly.

At each pause, freeze, review, and integration, update branch ownership, committed
and uncommitted work, imports and repairs, exact check results, review findings,
unavailable acceptance, blockers, and the next safe action. Add ledger and preview
revisions only after verification. Never commit pairing tokens, credentials, or
live database contents.

Publish the playbook, plan, generated index, JSON state, schema, and relevant
evidence as documentation-only checkpoints. Preserve unrelated staged work. Carry
the same documentation back to the integration branch so instructions do not
contradict each other.

On resume, read this index and the selected batch evidence, then inspect current
Git state and review results. Update the JSON before starting a batch when its
prerequisites, base revision, or ownership changed. Regenerate this file with
`node scripts/upstream-progress.mjs --write`, and verify it with
`node scripts/upstream-progress.mjs --check`.
